title: Journal each approved purchase exactly once

blocks.text: Settlement reconciles the day against a journal: one line, with terminal, STAN and amount, for every purchase the server approved. After a busy Saturday the journal had a few lines twice and a few purchases not at all, and one line for a purchase whose transaction had failed after the approval.

`ApprovalJournal` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ApprovalJournal.java` sits in the chain after the authorizer, which has already put its response in the Context. Other participants come after it. Finish `prepare` and `commit`, marked `TODO`. A purchase (`0200`) the authorizer approved (`39` = `00`) gets exactly one line, and only if its transaction commits; anything else gets none. The journal is given (`journal()`). About eight lines in total.
The tests deploy real TransactionManagers with Q2, in the test's own JVM. One of them runs two sessions and holds two purchases side by side until both are past your `prepare`.

cases.says: an approved purchase whose transaction commits gets one journal line with its terminal, STAN and amount
one participant instance serves every session, so what commit needs comes from the Context, never from a field
prepare only decides; the line is written in commit, which never comes for a transaction a later participant aborts
a declined purchase commits like any other transaction but gets no line
an approved network message moves no money and gets no line

origin.section: 1.5.1 Spot the Problem: The Terminal Check

concepts: Work that must happen only if the whole transaction succeeds belongs in commit, which never comes when a later participant aborts.
The TransactionManager creates each participant once and every session calls it, so per-transaction state lives in the Context, never in fields.
